Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopSphere Inc. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone followed by your name and affiliation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopSphere Inc.'s third quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hayes, CEO; Taylor Kim, CFO; Morgan Lee, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; Casey Nguyen, CTO; and Jordan Ellis, CDO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hayes, CEO of ShopSphere Inc.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong third quarter performance, driven by our new product and service launches and robust seller performance metrics, including growth to 2.47 million active sellers. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV reaching $35.2 billion, up 22% year-over-year.

Our focus remains on evolving order frequency and changes in customer purchasing habits, where we hit 2.8 orders per active customer, up 12% year-over-year. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our SphereDash quick-commerce service, which we believe will significantly boost average order values through convenience bundles and capture more of the quick-delivery market.

We are investing heavily in logistics and shipping efficiency to counter supply chain disruptions. We are focused on improving operating expenses through better cost management. We are expanding our seller services and value-added services revenue streams. Finally, we are committed to optimizing our take rate through pricing discipline and mix shifts.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. Our third quarter revenue was $6.7 billion, an increase of 25% year-over-year, reflecting strong GMV growth and take rate expansion to 19.2%. Gross margin was 42%, driven by improved product mix from private-label lines like EcoThread and efficiencies in fulfillment costs. Operating expenses were $2.45 billion, representing 28.4% of revenue, down 210 basis points year-over-year due to leverage across fulfillment, marketing, and G&A.

Marketing spend was disciplined at $540 million, flat year-over-year, with customer acquisition costs falling 14% to $28, thanks to performance channels like TikTok Shop yielding 5.2x ROAS.

Let me expand on these results by diving into the key aspects shaping our performance. First, our new product and service launches have been a major growth driver, contributing about 18% to the quarter-over-quarter GMV increase. We're seeing great early traction on ShopSphere Personalize, our AI-driven recommendation engine; EcoThread, our sustainable apparel line; and SphereDash, our ultra-fast delivery service in select markets. ShopSphere Personalize, leveraging neural networks for real-time collaborative filtering and visual search, reached 3.2 million opt-ins, or 28% of active users, lifting conversions 15% to 3.6% and AOV 12% to $78, attributing $185 million in GMV. NPS is 72, though we're addressing privacy feedback with better opt-outs.

EcoThread, with 150 SKUs from recycled materials at lower price points, sold 450,000 units for $42 million at 55% margins, attaching to 35% of non-fashion orders and boosting apparel GMV 41%, strongest in North America. Reviews average 4.6 stars, with sizing tweaks underway using 3D scanning. SphereDash, in 12 U.S. metros and pilots in Singapore and Mumbai, captured 8% of local orders, adding $95 million GMV at $4.20 fulfillment cost, with NPS 78. U.S. drove 75% impact, APAC 15% with strong ROI. We're investing $150 million in AI and micro-DCs to hit 30% innovative GMV by next year, improving LTV:CAC to 3.8x.

Turning to seller performance metrics, we ended with 2.47 million active sellers—those with at least one sale in the last 90 days—up 28% year-over-year and 7% quarter-over-quarter. Average seller revenue hit $14,200 quarterly, up 12% YoY, annualizing to $57,000, powering 68% of GMV. North America has 1.28 million actives at $16,800 ASR; Europe 650,000 up 42% at $12,500; APAC 540,000 up 55% at $10,200; LATAM 80,000. AI Seller Optimizer boosted conversions 24%, FBN at 62% penetration, Pro tier 420,000 subs. We're prioritizing mid-market sellers for 65% GMV share, guiding Q4 to 2.65-2.75 million actives and $14,500-$15,000 ASR.

On order frequency, we achieved 2.8 orders per active customer over 90 days, up 12% YoY, offsetting 4% AOV dip to $58 and fueling 18% GMV growth. Repeats (6+ months) at 4.1 orders, up 15%, via NovaPrime-like perks; new customers at 1.2. North America up 14%, EMEA 10%, APAC 22%. Drivers include NovaRecs 2.0 for 21% cross-sell, loyalty perks, mobile reorders. We're scaling MFCs and GenAI for 20% lift, guiding Q4 to 2.9-3.0.

Logistics and shipping costs rose 18% to $620 million or 14.8% of revenue due to disruptions—ocean rates up 45%, air 22%. North America $8.45/order up 16% from port strikes; Europe €6.20 up 21% from Red Sea; APAC $5.80 up 11%. We diversified carriers, deployed OmniRoute for 17% mile savings, added micro-FCs with robots, nearshored 35%, targeting 12% of revenue by 2025.

Operating expenses show leverage at 28.4%, down 210 bps. Fulfillment $1.27 billion down 4% YoY per unit to $2.82 via automation in 75% of centers, dynamic routing saving $120 million. Marketing $540 million, CAC $28; Tech $295 million flat % with GenAI lifting conversions 11%; G&A $345 million down 7%. Fixed costs now 38%, guiding Q4 27.5-28.5%.

Seller services and value-added revenue hit $4.2 billion, up 28%, 32% of total at 52% margins. 68% sellers use services: FBN 42% by GMV, NexAds 55%, NexPay 72% on $28 billion TPV, analytics 48%. ARPU $1,520 up 15%. Added 220 bps to growth, North America 55% share up 25%, APAC 45%. NexAI Hub at 35% adoption, guiding Q4 $4.6-4.8 billion.

Finally, take rate at 19.2%, up 120 bps YoY from ads to 7.8%, fulfillment 5.4%, pricing hikes 50-100 bps in electronics/beauty, tiering for enterprises. Promotions shaved 20-30 bps but ROI strong; mix to grocery 28%; APAC 21.4%. Next-Gen platform adds 25 bps, guiding FY 19-19.5%.

Our net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.20 per share. We ended with $3.2 billion in cash and equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of revenue $26-27 billion, GMV $135-140 billion.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Lee to discuss operations.

Morgan Lee:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on supply chain resilience and fulfillment optimization amid disruptions. Our shipping times improved by 22% through AI routing, with OTIF at 88%. Fulfillment costs improved 12% per unit to $2.82. We are implementing robotic automation in 75% of centers and expanding micro-fulfillment to 450 facilities for 30-minute SLAs in urban areas.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Morgan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from social commerce campaigns on TikTok and Instagram, tying into EcoThread and SphereDash launches, and personalized ad bundles. Customer acquisition costs were $28, down 14%. Our brand awareness increased by 25% per surveys. We are focusing on ROAS optimization at 5.2x and high-LTV segments like wellness.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Nguyen.

Casey Nguyen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI personalization like ShopSphere Personalize and seller tools like AI Optimizer. Our website uptime was 99.99%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%, now 65% of orders. We're investing in GenAI for recommendations and blockchain for supply chain visibility.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Ellis.

Jordan Ellis:
Thanks, Casey. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates because of ShopSphere Personalize and NovaRecs. We are also focusing on data privacy initiatives with GDPR opt-outs and explainability to address feedback.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will be conducting a question and answer session. [Operator instructions]. Our first question comes from Sarah Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Chen:
Thanks. On new launches, can you elaborate on SphereDash economics and regional rollout risks?

Jordan Hayes:
Thanks, Sarah. SphereDash is delivering strong early metrics—$95 million incremental GMV, 2.1x AOV premium, $4.20 cost 15% below benchmarks via predictive Kafka streams. NPS 78 with 92% repeat intent. U.S. metros strong, APAC pilots scaling with 3x India ROI despite higher CAC, offset by low churn. Regulatory hurdles in Europe delayed but privacy updates on track for 2025 expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
Great, thanks. Thoughts on seller metrics amid competition—how sustainable is 28% active growth?

Taylor Kim:
Mike, our 2.47 million actives and $14,200 ASR reflect sticky tools like FBN at 62% and Pro tier. Mid-market focus drives 65% GMV, AI Optimizer lifts 35% for users. APAC 55% surge via Flipkart migrations. Q4 guide 25-30% growth assumes no tariffs, outpacing peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Wong:
On order frequency, how are you addressing AOV softness and APAC variability?

Morgan Lee:
Lisa, 2.8 frequency up 12% via personalization and Prime perks—repeats at 4.1 orders. AOV $58 reflects essentials shift, but bundles preserve it. APAC 22% lift from live-streaming, countering China hybrid trends with WeChat. Micro-FCs target daily orders.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with Barclays.

David Patel:
Thanks. Logistics costs up 18%—mitigation progress and Q4 outlook?

Riley Patel:
David, disruptions like Red Sea and ports hit hard, but diversification cut single-carrier reliance to 25%, OmniRoute saved 17% miles, nearshoring 35%. Per-order down sequentially, guiding mid-single digits growth Q3, 5-7% decline Q4 restores margins.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Tran with Bank of America.

Emily Tran:
OpEx leverage impressive—what's driving fulfillment efficiencies?

Casey Nguyen:
Emily, automation in 75% centers boosted throughput 35%, robots cut labor 7 points. Dynamic routing 15% yield gain, micro-FCs 14% last-mile savings. Regional density in NA strongest, APAC improving 10% QoQ.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with Citigroup.

Raj Singh:
Seller services at 32% revenue—adoption drivers and competitive moat?

Jordan Ellis:
Raj, 68% penetration, FBN 42%, NexAds 55% via AI bidding 22% ROAS boost. NexAI 35% beta cuts churn 18%, social integrations add 150K sellers. Pro tier lock-in vs. Shopify fragmentation, guiding 72% adoption.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Hayes for closing remarks.

Jordan Hayes:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
